quotes.text: The only thing remarkable about the sheets is that the uncommons sheet depicted at the link above has a blank spot in the top left corner.
Another variant of the sheet, auctioned recently on Ebay, replaces the gap with an Exeggutor:
The choice of which cards appear more frequently on the sheets appears more or less random (non-holo Flareon is more common than non-holo Jolteon and Vaporeon, for example).
The commons and uncommons sheets are different to accomodate striped collation without including duplicate cards in booster packs.
The rare and holo sheets may be the same as for the other variants, or they may be different.
The direction the cards are inserted into the packs varies sometimes within a set, i.e. one box may be left to right, top to bottom and another right to left, bottom to top.
Occasionally, cards are out of sequence, the most common “error” being when two cards are flipped in sequence.
not all commons in box apparently come from the same sheet, there are usually 2-3 stacks of commons getting inserted into packs alternatingly

quotes.text: No, the same odds. Basically a 1 in 3 chance of a foil card in a booster pack.
When the cards are printed, the number of foils is 1 in 3 packs. Some people get better odds, some get worse.
Same price as before, same odds for holos (1 in 33 cards approximately).
Why are there holo and non-holos in jungle and fossil? After hearing many people’s comments on not wanting to play with their holo cards from base set, we decided to make the rare’s in both forms.

How do you get a 1st edition promo card? Those are very difficult to find. Here’s why: The only 1st ed. promo I know about is the #1 promo Pikachu that was accidentally inserted into 1st ed. Jungle packs.

I recently bought some Jungle boosters and all the holofoils didn’t have the Jungle stamp why is that? You lucky dog, you are the honored recipient of WotC’s most recent misprint, enjoy them while you can.
